scope: The preserved b21 complete candidate owns the same modern Backpack/campaign/workspace/vessel fields as the current candidate and includes local road recovery and the jointly solved approaches. It passes 2618 source checks, complete Monaco assembly and native Baltimore junction driving. It remains an emergency save-compatible fallback with known desktop performance limitations, not a substitute for final candidate acceptance. Production 5.5.1 is the upgrade starting point. Before promotion, build and verify this exact fallback with production configuration and complete the released/candidate/fallback-write/candidate-return save roundtrip.

app/js/building-entry.js.review: Caller-owned scratch within footprint distance queries and scalar eligibility scanning. Preserves exact segment math, finite-point filtering, concave area order, bounds fallback, current edits and independent public results. No persistence or backend changes.

app/js/discovery/runtime.js.review: Guards unchanged text and three owned HTML sections using UI-instance state. Does not change finding/mission receipt writers, Journal, Backpack, campaign or account persistence. Same controls and changed-message updates verified by the first-session journey.

app/js/editable-world/runtime.js.review: Keeps the existing local/shared edit behavior and persistence formats. Routes street-source invalidation through a revision owner so edits during asynchronous compilation remain pending and stale products are rejected.

app/js/engine/vehicle-road-attitude.js.review: Four private double-precision JS height values replace one native buffer per NPC contact solve per frame. Sampling order, iterative contact math, reentrant callbacks, final pose and anomaly records are unchanged. No persistence change.

app/js/interiors.js.review: Prepares one detached museum material lease through the existing support and permission resolver. Admission, owned-home exclusions, player state and saved interior records keep their existing authorities. No save or service schema changes.

app/js/interiors/gallery-runtime.js.review: Awaits normal renderer buffer/texture preparation after exhibits and furniture settle. Added render timing belongs only to the live gallery state; Journal and exhibit save handling are unchanged.

app/js/interiors/museum-program-preparat.review: Recognizes existing catalog source IDs and awaits the existing lazy interior module under the current publication guard. No new destination, access permission, persistence or backend protocol.

app/js/interiors/scene-builder.js.review: Exports the existing failed-construction resource disposer for the detached program lease. Room geometry, doors, collisions and serialized content remain unchanged.

app/js/interiors/venue-program-preparati.review: New bounded transient renderer-program lease per world sequence. Cloned camera and detached lighting scene preserve outdoor ownership; reset disposes resources. No saved state.

app/js/living-world/navigation-graphs.js.review: Pedestrian and traffic compilation materialize temporary candidate rows from packed traversal storage. Existing access rules, sorting, budgets and published population graphs remain identical; only selected source features survive compilation.

app/js/map/earth-base.js.review: One private projection output per synchronous road/path painting pass. Exact canvas-command parity on small and large maps; no changes to visibility, colors, road data, imagery, coverage or saved settings.

app/js/physics/building-collision.js.review: Identical horizontal and vertical predicates, candidate order and collision responses. Rejects geographically distant colliders before evaluating vertical properties, reducing measured temporary allocation. No collision data, geometry, persistence or backend protocol changes. Exposes a synchronous region lease for camera probes while retaining the same narrow-phase solver. Out-of-range probes use ordinary queries; nested leases and exceptions release every scene reference. Expired probe callbacks reject use; large scratch arrays are not retained. Region state is private to one synchronous callback and never persists across frames.

app/js/reality-capture/rdt-building-inde.review: Cooperative construction/validation of a transient nearest-building index. Preserves identity/coordinate edit detection, nearest ordering and cancellation. No saved data.

app/js/reality-capture/runtime.js.review: Awaits bounded capture selection under world/refresh/list identity guards. Same approved-representation endpoint and publication contract; no persistence changes.

app/js/runtime/core-frame-systems.js.review: Prepares resident renderer resources and the supported museum before first play; suspends unfinished outdoor preparation in interiors. Restores renderer target and preserves published geometry, input, movement and save ownership.

app/js/runtime/resident-presentation-pre.review: New normal-renderer one-pixel upload preparation. Restores viewport, scissor, visibility, culling and shadow flags in finally. No private renderer changes, gameplay data or persistence.

app/js/structure-semantics.js.review: Passes explicit optional compilation storage through to the existing canonical profile compiler. Standalone callers retain independent storage. No saved fields or protocol change.

app/js/structure-semantics/classificatio.review: Preserves an explicit service=parking_aisle distinction in derived structure semantics. Does not alter source tags, tunnel classification, topology or persisted fields.

app/js/structure-semantics/geometry.js.review: Polyline distance arithmetic and Float32 rounding are unchanged. The caller can explicitly provide temporary storage; ordinary callers retain independent arrays. No geometry or persistence semantics change.

app/js/structure-semantics/numeric-publi.review: Append-only bounded publication pages owned by a compilation. Published views are disjoint and never recycled or detached; only the current page is held by the allocator. No persisted fields or transport topology change.

app/js/structure-semantics/numeric-scrat.review: Bounded, explicitly borrowed numeric scratch pages for synchronous compilation. Nested calls have separate pages; completed profiles use independent publication buffers. At most one MiB is retained by each compiler pool. No saved data or network change.

app/js/terrain/far-field-mapped-context..review: Each loaded land/water context owns bounded append-only pages for immutable ring acceleration data. Release drops only allocator references; retained views are never recycled or detached. Geometry, holes, land classification and coverage unchanged. Normal regional land now uses its indexed Float64 coordinates as the sole stored polygon representation. Optional frozen outer/hole views preserve exact coordinates and inspection/serialization; queries preserve holes, bounds, ordering, explicit replacements and malformed-source fallback. Water, roads, structures, persistence and server contracts are unchanged.

app/js/terrain/far-field.js.review: Smaller frustum-culling cells for the same complete regional instance population. No geometry source, collision, identifier or save changes.

app/js/terrain/geographic-ring-index.js.review: Optional append-only publication storage for the same Float64 geographic edges and Uint32 bins. Exact crossing expressions and fallback order preserved; immutable edge count avoids retaining the input ring. No data/coverage/save changes. Optional coordinate inspection reconstructs frozen numeric pairs from the same Float64 endpoints; it does not retain provider/source arrays. Default water and legacy callers remain unchanged, including degenerate rings and publication lifetime.

app/js/terrain/location-world.js.review: Comment clarifies the shared terrain owner; publication order and ten-second wait are unchanged. No persisted data or geometry change.

app/js/terrain/rebuild.js.review: Published Float32 road-width samples use bounded append-only pages scoped to terrain publication and preserved through later region arrivals. Width calculation, rounding, rendered/physical road surfaces and region retirement unchanged. Unmarked ground roads additionally release temporary dense lane-marking samples; canonical roads, road-index ordering, rendered surfaces and collision coverage remain unchanged.

app/js/terrain/street-frontage-grading.j.review: Terrain opts into the shared frontage policy numeric snapshot. Existing outer-distance, ray occlusion, sampling, publication replacement and disposal rules remain authoritative. No road geometry, terrain datum, persistence or backend changes.

app/js/terrain/surface-decal-projection..review: Same clipping math, ordering and tolerances. Logical scratch lengths retain capacity; explicit workspaces borrow reusable Float64 storage while ordinary callers keep independent arrays. 1000 before/after geometry cases match exactly and sampled temporary allocation falls 90.9 percent in the isolated clipper. No saved data or physical surface policy changes.

app/js/terrain/tile-request-lifecycle.js.review: Consumer deadlines and AbortSignals retire only their own subscriptions. The existing cache owner retains actual source timeout, retry, eviction and world teardown. Transient loading behavior only; no saved fields or network protocol changes.

app/js/terrain/tiles.js.review: Uses the subscription-only waiter and removes the conflicting 2.4-second consumer failure authority. Actual source deadline, three-attempt retry ceiling, cache limit and generation teardown stay unchanged. No saved data.

app/js/ui/loading-progress.js.review: Reallocates player-facing loading progress to actual initial scenery completion. Rotating tips, location selection and saved settings are unchanged; no save schema.

app/js/urban-sandbox/player-position.js.review: Resolve the ground player from the occupied vehicle or selected walk/drive mode, rather than the existence of an inactive allocated walker. Preserves startup car fallback and distinguishes remote camera focus from the physical body. No saved schema or migration change.

app/js/urban-sandbox/runtime.js.review: Mapped storefront approach checks request exact-point walking validation and continue their existing local candidate search instead of resolving to another street. Store stock, wallet, Backpack, commerce transactions and saved state are unchanged. Civic incidents, witnesses and pursuit now follow the active ground-player owner; the inactive walker cannot substitute for the moving starter car. Occupied-vehicle authority and saved formats are unchanged. Scalar nearest-furniture selection preserves ties, radius and current eligibility; an installed interaction router owns its null result, avoiding a duplicate provider search. No persistence changes.

app/js/walking/camera-collision.js.review: Walking camera shares one synchronous candidate region across its unchanged sample positions. Every sample retains the existing height, footprint, guardrail and clearance rules. Fallback collision providers keep the prior point-query path. Exact comparisons cover mapped cell boundaries, elevated floors, open/closed doors and vegetation/interior isolation. No persistence, scene coverage or backend change.

app/js/world/building-body-geometry.js.review: Uses optional bounded private construction storage with disjoint attribute views. Exact geometry bytes, normals, UVs, transforms, footprint data, clones and edit behavior are preserved. No saved data.

app/js/world/building-facade-layout.js.review: Uses the geometry-owned construction allocator when available, preserving separate ranges, all facade values, and independently owned standalone publication. No visual, persistent or backend schema changes. Facade attribute writes now avoid per-triangle/per-vertex temporary arrays; 24 captured before/after byte fixtures preserve geometry attributes and facade plans exactly.

app/js/world/compiler/accepted-ground-se.review: Reconciles accepted complete overlapping transport geometry across roads and pedestrian/connector collections after ground selection. Only transient world publication ownership changes; missing, partial and rejected sources retain fallback coverage. No saved schema or transaction changes.

app/js/world/compiler/ordinary-street-pr.review: The same ordinary-street alignment solver receives an explicit optional storage allocator. Exact Float32/Float64 values and grade rules remain unchanged; no persistent fields change.

app/js/world/compiler/street-frontage-po.review: Exact Float64 frontage endpoint pages and numeric bucket IDs replace terrain-only retained edge/bounds object graphs. Geometry consumers retain stable objects; full materialization releases alternate buffers. Shared query order, roundoff tolerance, exclusions and section semantics verified across scales, translations and publication lifetimes. No new save fields or backend protocol.

app/js/world/compiler/street-pavement-fi.review: Retains the conservative source identity and adds exact compiled-product identity including cell bounds, units, curb packaging, polygons, markings, ramps and every ordered terrain-fitting segment input. Remote source context may change only when the actual product is equal; real geometry or height inputs invalidate reuse. No source-selection or persisted-schema change.

app/js/world/compiler/street-pavement-wo.review: Retains exact compilation, transferred numeric indexing and cached-first ordering. On a changed source key, compares the exact compiled surface product before repeating meshing/fitting. Only a matching product advertises a previously fitted surface; rejected or evicted reuse reconstructs through the original compiler. Compact metadata includes the complete height inputs and current diagnostic counts. No saved or backend data change.

app/js/world/compiler/transport-junction.review: Uses the accepted physical connection graph for shared road heights across source providers. Rejects missing, incomplete or unconnected height owners. Runtime world surfaces rebuild per location; persisted player records and save versioning are unchanged. Rolling back restores the earlier road geometry and its known limitations.

app/js/world/compiler/transport-network-.review: Prevents the expanded mixed-source endpoint match from connecting explicitly different at-grade levels. Transient topology only; same source identifiers and saved-data owners.

app/js/world/compiler/transport-structur.review: Parking tunnel specification reads the canonical parking clearance. Other road/bridge specifications are unchanged. Derived model only; no persistence or backend changes.

app/js/world/compiler/transport-surface-.review: Temporary solver storage remains scoped scratch; initial and reconciled published profiles can use bounded append-only pages without aliasing or detaching. Final packed profiles retain all numeric fields. Tunnel terrain probes use the corrected shared physical roof footprint. No saved data or protocol changes.

The same surface, bridge and tunnel solvers receive explicit scratch allocation. Computation order and numeric precision are unchanged; published output is copied before scratch reuse. No persistence change.

app/js/world/compiler/tunnel-envelope.js.review: Parking passages use the existing minimum walkable clearance independently of burial depth. Roof sweep width now matches the actual 2 cm lining offset plus 35 cm portal rim, instead of a fictitious 95 cm envelope. No source data or saved fields change.

app/js/world/compiler/tunnel-obstruction.review: Foundation and overhead-road overlap use the shared physical roof envelope. Buildings actually touched by the shell retain hard clearance bounds; adjacent buildings outside it no longer depress connected streets. No persisted fields change.

app/js/world/compiler/tunnel-system-mode.review: Containment and portal placement use the same corrected roof extent as obstruction and profile compilation. Existing shell/portal authority and data ownership remain intact; no persistence change.

app/js/world/fixed-regional-structures.j.review: Retires generalized transport geometry only when complete accepted exact coverage is proven, including curved approaches and pedestrian structures. Explicit layers, incomplete/parallel geometry and missing-source fallbacks remain. No player data mutation or migration.

app/js/world/linear-feature-presentation.review: Yields between individually clipped paths and bounded numeric copy loops. Same complete rendered geometry and terrain/road authority; transient scheduling only.

app/js/world/load-building-pass.js.review: Owns separate near/mid construction arenas, closes them on success or failure, and finalizes standalone attributes after batching. Complete world coverage, semantic rules, building identities and saved data remain unchanged.

app/js/world/load-geometry.js.review: Passes the optional construction arena into generated mid-LOD bodies and their existing fallback. It does not change geometry, material selection, location identity or saved state.

app/js/world/load-linear-runtime.js.review: Immediate linear-feature compilation passes a bounded publication store explicitly to each record. Standalone additions remain independently allocated. All feature identity/access/topology and saved data are unchanged.

app/js/world/load-reset.js.review: Disposes the transient museum program lease and clears its diagnostic result at world replacement. Existing player/save reset responsibilities are unchanged.

app/js/world/load-road-pass.js.review: Initial road compilation uses a pass-owned bounded publication store across cooperative yields. All accepted profiles and source coverage are retained; no player data or road identity changes.

app/js/world/load-roads.js.review: Creates the retained facility terrain callback in the stable loader scope instead of the per-load source context. Same dynamic terrain method, arguments, receiver and return value. Current-source retained-allocation comparison releases about 128 MB including raw regional and building-provider records. No geometry, coverage, persisted state or backend contract changes; native pacing still requires verification.

app/js/world/load-runtime-session.js.review: Awaits initial street coverage and lazy museum rendering readiness before admitting gameplay, with publication/session cancellation and normal failure handling. Does not alter saved location, travel, inventory or backend formats.

app/js/world/navigation.js.review: Keep nearest-road winner scalars until the scan completes instead of allocating discarded intermediate results. Same projection, height, continuity and bridge/tunnel transition rules, final result shape and search bounds. No geometry, identifiers or persisted state changes.

app/js/world/pavement-batch-ownership.js.review: New bounded active-publication ownership helper. A batch geometry and exact contact index share an idempotent reference-counted lease across an atomic handover. Last release disposes both; cancellation cannot dispose another publication’s resources. Numeric spatial lookup checks neighboring batches for original Float32 boundary tolerance and chooses the same highest contact as the original combined index. Does not retain prior publication objects or create a persistent cache.

app/js/world/pavement-materials.js.review: Transient, per-world pavement material ownership. Same three material parameters and concrete texture bytes; one shared set during overlapping construction/publication, idempotent per-lease release and final-owner disposal. World sequence or borrowed-map identity changes create a distinct set; external normal/roughness textures are never disposed here. Partial construction releases its own resources. No saved fields, permissions, data migration or backend protocol changes.

app/js/world/pavement-terrain-conformanc.review: Fast checkpoints remain synchronous until their existing work budget is exhausted. Exact geometry and cancellation remain unchanged; the isolated 5000-triangle comparison reduces Promise creation from 10005 to two. No persistence or backend fields change. Browser pacing remains separately required.

app/js/world/pavement-terrain-partition..review: One clipping workspace per iterator; copies borrowed coordinates into published output and ordinary arrays for failure diagnostics. Interleaved iterators and retained diagnostics remain independent. No geometry, coverage tolerance or saved-field changes.

app/js/world/retired-building-buffers.js.review: Private construction ranges share bounded pages until their geometry owners retire. Unbatched survivors copy exact attribute bytes into independent storage, preventing page pinning; final batches, clones and neighboring geometry remain valid. No persistence or building identity changes.

app/js/world/spawn.js.review: Exact-point walking validation can reject an unsafe local interaction without searching for a remote arrival. Ordinary arrival fallback, drive/bridge/tunnel support, actor/save formats and persisted poses are unchanged.

app/js/world/street-interior-suspension..review: Cancels only unfinished preparation while retaining accepted contact and coverage. Cancellation preserves existing source/terrain invalidation without inventing invalidation of valid accepted detail; missing first coverage stays retryable. No persistent data.

app/js/world/street-overview.js.review: Same complete source domain and masks; initial loading awaits all cells and mapped-path completion, while travel retains incremental scheduling. Cancellation and source identities remain guarded. No persistent data or source coverage reduction.

app/js/world/street-packet-cache.js.review: Retains one bounded 16 MiB cache with private arrays and exact physical owner checks. Revalidates an existing fitted surface only when both its previous source key and exact product identity match under the current owner. Updates metadata and byte accounting atomically; eviction and owner changes force reconstruction. No second geometry cache or persistent format.

app/js/world/street-pavement-runtime.js.review: Retains generation/revision cancellation, exact terrain/portal fitting, canonical face order and atomic publication. Validates changed-source reuse against the worker product identity and existing physical owners. Unchanged 128-unit render batches retain geometry and their exact walking-contact index through publication leases. Changed batches rebuild through the existing worker indexer; mapped ground keeps its bounded index. Composite sampling preserves maximum height and boundary tolerance. Failure or cancellation releases only staged leases; the old publication remains usable. Material leases and isolated publication callbacks preserve program lifetime without retaining old publications. No road/bridge/tunnel authority, coverage, save or backend change. Invalidation now survives pending/cancelled work until a current publication commits; editable source revision joins ground/world/generation guards to reject stale source edits.

app/js/world/street-source-input.js.review: Includes the existing road surfaceBias in the compact worker snapshot because it is consumed by the terrain height sampler and therefore must participate in cache invalidation. Source selection, global road identities and all gameplay/save data are unchanged.

app/js/world/street-source-revision.js.review: Versions editable frontage/source mutations independently from physical terrain changes so cooperative street construction cannot publish over a newer edit. In-memory ownership only; no saved format or authority change.

app/js/world/structure-aware.js.review: One explicit append-only publication store per structure compilation, shared across provisional reconciliation passes and released after final packing. No global allocation owner or terrain/topology policy changes. No persistence changes.

app/js/world/traversal-graph-storage.js.review: New packed storage for published navigation nodes and segments uses Float64 values and Uint32 IDs. Endpoint and feature references retain their existing owners. Temporary row views are limited to queries or pedestrian/traffic compilation; no persistent graph/save format migration.

app/js/world/traversal-segment-index.js.review: The same broad phase reads either packed published segments or explicit row fixtures. Cell membership, broad segments, sorted original IDs, limits and cache invalidation remain unchanged.

app/js/world/traversal.js.review: Navigation compilation retains exact Float64 node coordinates and packed segment facts. Route search and nearest-feature selection preserve source references, ordering, costs, direction/access and graph invalidation. No saved data changes.

app/js/world/vector-resolution-ownership.review: Adds an opt-in curved-segment coverage proof for fixed regional conflation. Default ordinary vector-road matching is unchanged. Pure geometry ownership; no save fields.

config/context-write-allowlist.json.review: Registers the reviewed transient renderer and street owners. Moves editable frontage invalidation writes to the explicit street-source revision owner; no permission, service rule or persisted schema change.

config/performance-budgets.json.review: Reviewed verification policy only: 30FPS floor,35ms p95 scheduling allowance and existing50ms p99/individual-pause/hitch limits. Existing byte/request caps apply per cold load,bounded travel,each reload and finalization with complete cumulative accounting. This configuration is not shipped and changes no runtime/save/backend format. The explicit policy change and retained failed evidence are documented in docs/release-review/2026-10-19/VERIFICATION-MEASUREMENT-SCOPE.md.

config/scene-resource-budgets.json.review: Evidence-backed named Baltimore collider baseline for authored quay/venue fixtures and repaired approaches. No runtime or save protocol change; timing, coverage and retention gates remain unchanged.

config/system-release-gates.json.review: Extends only the complete performance process deadline from 40 to 60 minutes to accommodate 930 seconds of movement, twelve full reloads and mobile checks. Individual timing, coverage, retention and loading criteria are unchanged. Verification scheduling only; no runtime, backend or save format change.

scripts/lib/release-source-identity.mjs.review: Release verification only: read-only Git invocations disable optional index refresh locks and preloadIndex to avoid filesystem contention. Strict dirty/untracked/commit identity comparisons and the original 10-second timeout remain. This helper does not ship in the browser or alter saved data, runtime schemas or service protocols. It is conservatively included because unknown script inputs are classified as runtime.
